related_questions.question: Who qualifies for student loan forgiveness?

text_blocks.snippet: Generally, federal student loan forgiveness programs primarily benefit those employed in public service or those with disabilities. The most prominent program, Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), forgives remaining loan balances for borrowers with Direct Loans who work full-time for qualifying government or non-profit organizations after making 120 qualifying monthly payments. Additionally, borrowers with disabilities may qualify for a Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) discharge.

list.title: Qualifying Employers:
list.snippet: Federal, state, local, or tribal government agencies, or qualifying non-profit organizations.

list.title: Qualifying Loans:
list.snippet: Direct Loans (or loans consolidated into a Direct Consolidation Loan).

list.title: Qualifying Payments:
list.snippet: 120 monthly payments (need not be consecutive) while working full-time for a qualifying employer.

list.title: Repayment Plan:
list.snippet: Must be on an income-driven repayment plan or the standard 10-year repayment plan.

list.title: Eligibility:
list.snippet: Borrowers who are eligible for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) may qualify for a TPD discharge.

list.title: Documentation:
list.snippet: Requires documentation showing the borrower meets specific disability criteria, often related to their Social Security disability determination.

list.title: Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) Forgiveness:
list.snippet: Under IDR plans, any remaining balance on federal student loans may be forgiven after 20 or 25 years of qualifying payments.

list.title: Teacher Loan Forgiveness:
list.snippet: Certain teachers may be eligible for loan forgiveness after meeting specific requirements, such as teaching full-time for five consecutive years at a low-income school.
Consolidation: If your loans are not Direct Loans, you may need to consolidate them into a Direct Consolidation Loan to qualify for PSLF or IDR forgiveness.
Tax Implications: Forgiven loan amounts may be considered taxable income in some cases.
Consult Resources: Federal Student Aid (studentaid.gov) is a valuable resource for detailed information on all federal student loan forgiveness programs.
